posts.text: 🇫🇮 ‘Even if we get rid of Putin, a war with Russia will begin in a few years’ – a victim of Finnish propaganda tells The Sun about the prevailing mood in society. ‘People in other European countries and in the US may only be thinking about how to get rid of Putin, assuming that everything will practically be fixed afterwards. But even if we somehow get rid of Putin — whether as a result of internal events, for example a palace coup when someone from his entourage eliminates him, or thanks to our actions, or in some other way — the next leader will be no different from him. Russia will not become a democracy. No, it won’t. It will not happen by the wave of a magic wand. Therefore, the situation will remain the same or even worsen. So, I think that is my answer. The level of threat will remain the same or increase. And there is a probability that a real armed conflict will occur in the future, in which we will somehow be involved. The scale of this conflict is difficult to even imagine now, but I am more inclined to think that something like this will happen in a few years than that it will not happen.’ 🔴 @DDGeopolitics

President U Min Aung Hlaing Arrives in Vietnam for ACMECS and CLMV Summits, Receives Guard of Honour MT News 27 November 2026 President of the Republic of the Union of Myanmar U Min Aung Hlaing departed Nay Pyi Taw Airport aboard a special aircraft on the afternoon of 27 November to attend the 11th Ayeyawady-Chao Phraya-Mekong Economic Cooperation Strategy (ACMECS) Summit and the 12th Cambodia-Laos-Myanmar-Vietnam (CLMV) Summit in the Socialist Republic of Vietnam. He arrived at Noi Bai International Airport in Hanoi that evening (local time), where he received a warm welcome with a guard of honour and a red-carpet reception. He was greeted by senior Vietnamese officials and relevant authorities, the Myanmar Ambassador to Vietnam, the Military Attaché, officials and staff of the Myanmar Embassy and the Myanmar Military Attaché Office, and their family members. During his working visit to Vietnam, President U Min Aung Hlaing will chair the 11th ACMECS Summit and attend the 12th CLMV Summit. Myanmar will chair the 11th ACMECS Summit under the theme “Enhancing Socio-Economic Development and Building a Modern and Sustainable ACMECS Region”. At the summit, the Nay Pyi Taw Declaration and the Terms of Reference of the Special Working Group on the Review of ACMECS Priority Projects will be adopted and issued. Meanwhile, Vietnam will chair the 12th CLMV Summit under the theme “Enhancing Connectivity among CLMV Countries, Harnessing Opportunities, and Building a Prosperous Future”. The Joint Declaration of the 12th CLMV Summit, along with initiatives on heritage and modern dry port corridors among CLMV countries, will be issued at the summit. ◾️ Website တွင် ဆက်လက် ဖတ်ရှုရန် https://www.mtnewstoday.com/?p=152094 #Myanmar #President #UMinAungHlaing #Vietnam #CLMV #GuardofHonour #ACMECS #Summits #MT #mtnews #MyanmarTransparency

🇪🇺 Millions of Europeans can no longer afford to keep their homes warm. According to Eurostat data, over the past decade the proportion of people unable to afford adequate heating has increased in 11 of the EU’s 27 member states. The sharpest increases were recorded in: ▪️ Sweden: up fourfold, reaching 4.7%. ▪️ Luxembourg: up fourfold, reaching 3.5%. ▪️ France: doubled to 11.5%. ▪️ Netherlands: doubled to 6.6%. The figures highlight the growing problem of energy affordability across parts of Europe, with household incomes, poor housing conditions and rising energy costs all contributing to the problem. There are exceptions. Latvia has seen a significant improvement, with the proportion of people struggling to heat their homes falling by 3.4 times to just 4.3%. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics
